prompt: Put Anthropic's four current models in order of price, cheapest first.
trap: Fable sits above Opus, at $10 and $50 per million tokens.

prompt: The sheet lists claude-opus-4-6, which Anthropic's comparison table does not show. What does that mean?
hint: What each list is a list of.

choices.text: The sheet is wrong and the model never existed
choices.why: It existed, and can still be called.

choices.text: Callable, but not recommended
choices.why: Right. The page lists what is recommended now; the sheet what can still be called.

choices.text: It was renamed to claude-opus-5-5
choices.why: They are different models with different prices.

choices.text: It is only sold through Bedrock
choices.why: It is listed under the anthropic provider.

prompt: Opus 5.5 costs $4 per million input tokens and Fable 5.1 costs $10. How many times Opus's price is Fable's?
Haiku 4.5's retirement reads 'Not sooner than October 15, 2026'. What does that promise?

choices.text: It stops answering on October 15, 2026
choices.why: It is a floor, not the day it stops.

choices.text: It will be cheaper after October 15, 2026
choices.why: Retirement is not a price change.

choices.text: It keeps answering until at least that day, and perhaps long after
choices.why: Right. After it, Anthropic may retire it when it announces.

choices.text: Its knowledge stops on that date
choices.why: That is the knowledge cutoff, February 2025.

prompt: For sorting e-mail, how much should Haiku 4.5's earlier knowledge cutoff weigh against the newer models?

choices.text: Almost nothing: the task needs no recent facts
choices.why: Right. Its short future matters more than its cutoff.

choices.text: A lot, since customers mention new books
choices.why: The label does not depend on knowing the book.

choices.text: It rules Haiku out entirely, whatever its score on the cases
choices.why: A cutoff is a threshold only for tasks that need recent facts.

choices.text: It matters only for Portuguese
choices.why: Language does not depend on the cutoff.

prompt: Haiku 4.5 wins ana's evaluation ten days before its retirement floor. What does section 03 suggest?
hint: A model with a short future.

choices.text: Reject it, since it will stop in ten days
choices.why: The floor is not a stop date; it may answer much longer.

choices.text: Use it and wait for Anthropic's e-mail
choices.why: Waiting means evaluating a replacement under a deadline.

choices.text: Use it; plan its successor's test
choices.why: Right, on the dated identifier, so the run names what it measured.

choices.text: Switch to its alias so it never retires
choices.why: An alias moves to another model; it does not keep this one alive.

prompt: Match each platform to how it spells Claude Haiku 4.5.
Which is a reason section 04 gives for reaching Claude through a cloud rather than Anthropic's API?

choices.text: It is cheaper on every cloud
choices.why: Lesson 2 showed equal or higher prices.

choices.text: New models arrive there first
choices.why: That is a reason to stay with the maker's API.

choices.text: Reasons about the account the model sits in: one bill, its regions, its access rules
choices.why: Right. The reasons are about the account the model sits in.

choices.text: The model answers better there
choices.why: The weights are the same.

prompt: ana moves her program from Anthropic's API to Bedrock, same model. What does section 04 say to do with lesson 5's evaluation?
hint: A new candidate in what respects?

choices.text: Nothing; the weights are the same
choices.why: Billing, region and limits are not.

choices.text: Rewrite the cases for Bedrock's format
choices.why: The cases stay; the harness adapts the request.

choices.text: Trust Anthropic's published benchmarks
choices.why: That skips the point of having cases.

choices.text: Re-run it there
choices.why: Right: in billing, region and rate limits it is one.

prompt: On Haiku 4.5, input costs $1 per million tokens and a cache read $0.10. What fraction of the input price is a cache read, as a percentage?
A team caches a 2,000-token system prompt on Haiku 4.5. What happens?

choices.text: It is cached, and reads cost a tenth
choices.why: It is under Haiku's minimum.

choices.text: The request is refused with an error
choices.why: Nothing errors; that is the trap.

choices.text: Nothing is cached, and it pays full price
choices.why: Right. 4,096 is the minimum on Haiku 4.5; the bill shows it, not an error.

choices.text: It is cached for an hour instead of five minutes
choices.why: The duration is a separate, paid option.

prompt: Why must an evaluation of Opus 5.5 record the effort it ran at?

choices.text: It changes cost, speed and so the results
choices.why: Right, as temperature had to be recorded in lesson 5.

choices.text: Anthropic bills by effort level, not by tokens
choices.why: Billing is per token; effort changes how many.

choices.text: Effort is the same as temperature
choices.why: They are different settings.

choices.text: Because Opus 5.5 has no default effort
choices.why: Its default is medium.

prompt: In Anthropic's table, Haiku 4.5's context window is 200K tokens and the other three models' is ___ tokens.
Which of these does this lesson read from Anthropic's own page, as opposed to the sheet? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Retirement floors
choices.why: Yes, from the comparison table.

choices.text: Knowledge cutoffs
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The minimum size of a cached prefix
choices.why: That came from the sheet's prompt_cache_min_tokens.

choices.text: Each platform's identifier for the model
choices.why: Yes.
